objects.title: Replenishment vs Subscription
objects.summary: Within the HygieneRoll model, a subscription is a recurring commerce arrangement, while replenishment is planning around an item approaching renewed need.

claims.text: Within the HygieneRoll model, a subscription describes a recurring commerce arrangement, and replenishment describes planning around an item approaching renewed need or depletion.

objects.title: Household Depletion Clock
objects.summary: The HygieneRoll model represents each household essential as an independent replenishment clock.

claims.text: The HygieneRoll model represents a household as containing multiple recurring essentials whose supply can deplete on different timelines, and it treats each item as an independent replenishment clock.

objects.title: Planning Trigger
objects.summary: In calculator v0.1, the planning trigger is rounded depletion timing minus lead time and safety buffer, clamped at zero.

claims.text: In HygieneRoll calculator v0.1, the planning trigger is the rounded depletion timing minus lead time minus safety buffer, clamped at zero. It is a scenario-derived planning threshold.

objects.title: Lead Time and Safety Buffer
objects.summary: Lead time and safety buffer are separate user-supplied planning inputs in calculator v0.1.

claims.text: Within HygieneRoll calculator v0.1, lead time is the time assumed between initiating replenishment and availability or arrival.

Within HygieneRoll calculator v0.1, the safety buffer is a user-selected additional time before estimated depletion. It is not a medically safe stock level, an industry optimum, or a statistical confidence interval.

objects.title: Illustrative Cadence
objects.summary: Illustrative cadence estimates how long a replenishment quantity would cover under the visitor's own usage assumptions.

claims.text: Within HygieneRoll calculator v0.1, illustrative cadence estimates how long a replenishment quantity would cover under the supplied usage assumptions. It is not an optimal subscription frequency, an automatic shipping recommendation, or a guaranteed usage interval.

objects.title: Ownership of Return
objects.summary: Ownership of return describes control of the consumer-facing re-entry surface through which recurring household demand can come back.

claims.text: Within HygieneRoll, ownership of return describes controlling or directly operating the consumer-facing re-entry surface through which recurring household demand can come back. It does not mean legal ownership of consumers, ownership of their behavior, proven retention, or guaranteed recurring revenue.

objects.title: Re-entry
objects.summary: Re-entry is the conceptual return to a consumer surface as a recurring need approaches again.

claims.text: Within the HygieneRoll model, re-entry is the point at which a household returns to a consumer surface because a recurring need is approaching again. It is distinct from a first purchase.

objects.title: Category Expansion
objects.summary: HygieneRoll's category model starts with paper hygiene as the entry anchor and extends toward personal care and household hygiene.

claims.text: The HygieneRoll category model treats paper hygiene as the clearest entry anchor, then personal care, then broader household hygiene. Paper hygiene is not the category ceiling. This sequence is a strategic model, not a claim that it is the empirically best expansion path.
